newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian teachers flee after Java riots.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian teachers flee after Java riots.

text.p: Hundreds of government teachers have fled Indonesia's Sampang region in east Java province after election-related riots last month, the official Antara news agency reported on Tuesday.
The riots were sparked by reports that the ruling Golkar party was sweeping general elections, Antara said.
"After the riots on May 29, hundreds of teachers have fled for fear of their safety. In addition, many of them have lost their houses because they have been burned by the people," said Antara.
Hundreds of supporters of the Moslem-based United Development Party (PPP) burned ballot boxes, shops and 24 teachers' houses in Sampang on Madura island, alleging election fraud.
The electoral commission held an unprecedented re-vote last week which Golkar also won.

Antara said more than 20 people have been arrested since the riots, but only four of those would face trial for unspecified crimes. Indonesian teachers working for government schools are automatically members of the Civil Servants Corps (KORPRI), who have to vote for Golkar. Golkar, in power for much of President Suharto's 30-year rule, swept the general election with more than 74 percent of the vote.
The PPP won just under 23 percent and the fragmented Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) took three percent of the poll to fill the 425 elected seats at the House of Representatives.
In Madura Golkar won 58 percent of the new ballots cast and the PPP 41.1 percent.
Antara said police had been deployed to supervise the final examinations at at least 489 elementary schools throughout Sampang regency because of the absence of teachers. It gave no further details.
It quoted Moh Bakir, chief of the Sampang office of the education ministry, as saying on Monday the teachers would be given protection once they decided to teach again.
He said the teachers might also be transferred to other cities if they could not cope.
